decisions.reason: The accessibility constraint narrows the existing general connector-placement flexibility by requiring the battery connector to remain usable beside the case-mounted USB-C opening.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Thanks for sharing, everything looks good, I can see only one potential issue. The connector above usb, probably battery since is is L shape and usb must go through case opening then we will not be able to plug the battery cable in it as case will get in the way.

value_updates.connector_edge_flexibility: Connectors may be placed across the proposed board sides as needed, provided the battery connector remains accessible for cable insertion when USB-C passes through the case opening.

decisions.reason: The source decision constrains battery-connector placement; it does not necessarily change the enclosure because relocating the connector can resolve the obstruction while the existing enclosure-adaptation requirement remains valid.
Mechanical accessibility of the battery connector does not change the AXP2101 electrical power path or charging behavior.
The source changes placement accessibility, not the connector series, pitch, pin count, pin functions, or mounting type.
The battery-connector clearance issue does not affect the required sensor-module connectors or their pinouts.
USB-C is mentioned only as a neighboring mechanical feature; the standalone regulator, activation condition, and 3.3V supply behavior remain unchanged.
The battery-connector accessibility constraint does not change the ESP32 module choice or breakout requirements.
The source contains no change to I2C cabling, pull-ups, bus speed, or signal conditioning.
Battery-connector placement relative to the enclosure does not affect the AXP2101 exposed-pad thermal requirement.
The source raises a mechanical-access issue and does not change component availability, cost, or sourcing policy.
The affected connector is the battery connector above USB-C, not the panel-mounted power-button connector or its control behavior.
The source does not alter USB-C enumeration or programming functionality; USB-C is referenced only to explain the physical obstruction.
